fields.meta_title: Overtime Request Form With Weekly Hour Checks | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create an overtime request form that totals the scheduled week and sends anything over your weekly cap to a manager. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Overtime Request Form That Checks the Hours
fields.hero_description: Build an overtime request form that adds the extra hours to each schedule and routes them to the right approver.
fields.features_heading: Every Field Checks a Number Your Policy Sets
fields.features_subheading: An overtime request form asks to work extra hours before they are worked. Here, each section checks a limit from your policy.
fields.feature_1:
The new weekly total, before sign-off

The form looks up the hours already on the person's schedule for that workweek and adds the request to them. The approver sees the new total beside the hours asked for.
fields.feature_2:
Limits written as your rules

Name the numbers your overtime policy uses, such as a weekly cap or a monthly hours budget. The form applies them to every request, and you change one by prompting again.
fields.feature_3:
A reason picked from your list

Requesters choose a reason you define, like covering an absence, and add a line of detail. The app's dashboard then counts overtime hours by reason for each department.
fields.feature_4:
Approvers set by department

Each request goes to the person who approves for that department, and one past a limit also goes to the next manager up. A reminder goes out if nobody answers in time.
fields.feature_5:
A deadline that fits your notice rule

Set how far ahead a request has to come in, such as 48 hours before the shift. Later requests still submit, marked late, and the approver sees how much notice there was.
fields.feature_6:
Requests in a database you own

Every request and its decision land in a database you own, with no response caps. Payroll filters the approved hours by pay period instead of collecting signed paper sheets.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Approve Extra Hours
fields.tab_content_1:
Cassius would reach 54 hours, which sends his line up a level

Drumlin Building Supply caps pickers at 50 hours a week. Shift lead Ottavia Mancuso asks 3 pickers for a 10-hour Saturday. Zebedee Okorie reaches 48 hours and Ffion Hargreaves 50, and both go to the supervisor. Cassius Nordqvist would reach 54 hours, and his line goes to operations manager Odhran Lowenstein.
fields.tab_content_2:
Fairlow Court has 9 of its 40 hours left for a 6-hour job

Hearthmoor Residential gives Fairlow Court a budget of 40 overtime hours a month. Maintenance tech Mateus Avelar asks for 6 hours on Sunday to replace a boiler pump. The building has used 31 and has 9 left. The request goes to property manager Lavinia Ebsworth alone. Past 40, the regional director signs too.
fields.tab_content_3:
Worked from 2:00 am to 5:30 am, filed at 7:10 am

The pump alarm at Ploughgate Water District went off at 2:00 am, and operator Ravindra Pradhan drove in to fix it with nobody awake to approve the time. He finished at 5:30 am. At 7:10 am he filed 3.5 hours from his phone as a call-in worked before approval, and the form sent it to supervisor Saskia Kovalenko to confirm.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three ask, and the one with 6 hours of overtime gets it

Eastmere Inn hands each extra shift to the volunteer with the fewest overtime hours this month. When 3 night auditors ask for the 8-hour Saturday audit, the form ranks them: Ignacio Tessaro at 6 hours, Thandiwe Wojcik at 9, then Rosalie Crowther at 14. It emails Ignacio that the shift is his.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an Overtime Request Form
fields.howto_description: These steps turn your written limits and approvers into an overtime request form that checks each request's hours before anyone signs.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the policy you follow now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the fields each request needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the overtime policy you already follow, including the weekly cap and who approves for each department. Settle any rule that lives only in a manager's head, since the form can only apply rules you can state.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start from the boxes on your current overtime request form PDF or paper sheet: the date, start time, end time, hours, and reason. Then add the fields paper never used, like the department, which decides who approves.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the form in plain English and put your real numbers in the prompt, such as a 45-hour weekly cap. Emergent builds the form from that prompt, along with its rules and the database behind it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: The weekly total needs the hours each person is already scheduled for. Keep the schedule in the app's own table, or connect the scheduling tool you use if it has an API. Match the form's week to the one payroll uses.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the approver for each department and the person who signs once a request passes a limit. Then set when a reminder goes out for a request nobody has answered, such as 4 hours before the shift starts.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Try it on last month's requests
fields.howto_step_6_des: Enter 6 requests from last month, including one that broke the cap and one call-in. Check that each reached the approver you expected and that the weekly totals match your timesheets for those weeks.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form and send the link to supervisors and staff, or pin it next to the schedule they already check. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What is an overtime request form?
faq_plan.a: An overtime request form is the record someone fills in to ask for approval before working past their regular schedule. It names the person, the date, the start and end time, the hours, and the reason, and it ends with the approver's decision. Payroll then has a dated record of which extra hours were approved and by whom.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an overtime request form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, and Emergent builds the form along with the database behind it. Name the weekly cap your policy sets and the approver for each department. Emergent builds the routing logic from that description: a request past the cap reaches a second approver without anyone forwarding it.

faq_plan.q: What fields should an overtime request form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the employee's name, department, date, start time, end time, total hours, and reason, plus the approver's decision and its date. A paper sheet or overtime request form PDF stops there. Add the pay period the hours fall in, which lets payroll filter by it, and a job code if overtime is charged to projects.

faq_plan.q: Should an overtime request form be separate from the form for time off?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Overtime asks to add hours beyond the schedule, while a time off request form asks to take hours off it, and each needs its own fields and sometimes its own approver. Keep them as two forms that share one employee list. A manager then sees someone's leave next to their extra shifts for the same week. In an app Emergent builds, both forms write to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What reasons should an overtime request form let people choose from?
faq_plan.a: Pull the choices from last year's overtime records, such as covering an absence, a customer deadline, a call-in, equipment failure, or seasonal volume, and add Other with a required note. Keep the list short enough to read without scrolling. Review the Other notes each quarter: a note that keeps coming back becomes its own choice.

faq_plan.q: How far in advance should an overtime request form be submitted?
faq_plan.a: That depends on your policy. Pick a period that gives the approver time to answer before the shift, such as two working days, and keep a same-day path for call-ins. Count the notice from the shift start: a request for a 6:00 am Monday shift filed at noon Sunday has 18 hours of notice. The app can send the approver a Slack or email reminder as the start time nears.

faq_plan.q: What should an overtime request form ask when someone will work late alone?
faq_plan.a: Ask where the person will be, when they expect to finish, whether anyone else will be on site, and who they will check in with when they leave. Confirm that the contact details on file are current before the shift. If they are out of date, link the request to your emergency contact form so the person can update them first.

faq_plan.q: How do I set a weekly hours cap on an overtime request form?
faq_plan.a: Write the cap into the prompt with an action, such as sending requests past 50 hours to a manager. The cap is your own rule: the FLSA sets no limit on the number of hours employees aged 16 and older may work in any workweek. The DOL describes a workweek as a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours. Start the form's week on the same day and hour as payroll's.

faq_plan.q: How should an overtime request form handle hours worked before approval?
faq_plan.a: Let people file them as hours already worked, with the start and end time, and route them to a supervisor to confirm. The DOL says an announcement that overtime will not be paid unless authorized in advance will not impair the employee's right to compensation for compensable overtime hours that are worked. A separate label shows how often call-ins skip the usual approval.

faq_plan.q: What should a warehouse overtime request form check before the shift?
faq_plan.a: Check two things before approval: that the extra hours keep the picker under your weekly cap, and that any equipment they will run has a current check. For a forklift driver, ask for the date of the last forklift inspection form and flag the request when today's check is missing. If schedules live in another tool with an API, the app Emergent builds can pull them in.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank paper: college and agency PDFs, a sample authorization sheet, a Scribd upload and a Pinterest board. Each asks for the date, the hours and a reason, then stops at a signature line. None knows how many hours the person already has on the schedule that week, how much of the department's overtime is left or what to do with hours someone already worked on a call-in. This page builds the form that does that checking before anyone signs, keeps every limit framed as the employer's own policy, and answers the setup questions (fields, notice, caps, after-the-fact hours) with dol.gov quotes where the law comes up and no wage-law advice.
